One named Kawanami contributes
the following article to the Nippo under the above heading:-
I extend my sympathy to the
Towa Theatre which was prohibited from exhibiting a Japanese
news film entitled "8,000 km of national defence line".
I agree with the action taken by the authorities who fear
that trouble might take place on the exhibition of such
a film, in view of the international situation in the
Settlement, but I am very sorry that we Japanese residents
are unable to view such a suitable film as we need a
knowledge of defence at this time of crisis.
I am displeased with the Municipal
administrative policy in connection with the ban placed on
the above mentioned film and the question of the film
entitled "New Earth". I do not know whether or not the
Chinese authorities asked the S.M.C. to interfere with
the exhibition of Japanese films, but we Japanese suffer
loss of dignity because although we enjoy extraterritorial
rights in the International Settlement, exhibition of
Japanese films at a Japanese theatre is interfered with.
In Chinese controlled territory films or plays which
instigate anti-Japanism, I believe, have been exhibited
and staged. Some may suggest that we should show the
magnanimous attitude of a great nation. In that case the
Chinese people should show a similar attitude. However
it is now not a question of attitude but of dignity. I
do not declare that the S.M.C. is deliberately supporting
the Chinese people and listening to their every want,
nevertheless the S.M.C. is in a position to request the
Chinese people to reflect.
Our Japanese authorities need
to pay attention to this matter. Why are we residents
unable to view our own film which is produced as part of

CASE AGAINST NATIONAL SALVATION ASSOCIATION LEADERS
OPENS

At 2 p.m. June 11, the Kiangsu High Court commenced the hearing of the case against Sung Chun-dz (沈鈞儒), Tsang Nai-ohi (章乃器), Tseu Tao-fun (鄒韜奮), Wong Zao-dz (王造時), Li Kung-poh, (李公樸), Soo Chi-li (沙千里) and Sz Liang (史良), who were arrested by the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government with the assistance of the Police of the International Settlement and French Concession in November last on a charge of endangering the internal security of the Republic of China.
Strict precautionary measures were adopted during the hearing of the case and in all about 300 gendarmes and policemen were on duty inside and outside the Court. With the exception of newspaper reporters and two relatives of each of the seven accused, nobody was permitted to witness the proceedings.
Messrs. Eugene Y.B. Kiang (江一平), Zing Lien-kwei (秦聯奎), Chen Ding-sai (陳霆銳) and sixteen other lawyers representing the seven accused were present.
After the reading over of the text of the charge sheet by the Procurator, Mr. Fang Ven (方聞), the Presiding Judge, ordered six accused to withdraw from the Court and commenced to interrogate Sung Chun-dz.

Sung Chun-dz's Statement

The following questions were put by the Presiding Judge to Sung Chun-dz:-
Q. How was the National Salvation Association formed?
A. After consideration had been given to local conditions in the various districts, steps were taken to organize University Professors' National Salvation Associations, Students' National Salvation Associations and Various Circles National Salvation Federations. This being done, the Various Circles National Salvation Federations in the various districts again appointed delegates to form a Various Circles National Salvation Federation.
Q. What was the procedure to become a member of the Association?
A. All those who were willing to resist Japan could participate.
Q. To which national salvation association did you belong?
A. The Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.
Q. When was the All-China National Salvation Association inaugurated?
A. It was inaugurated on May 31 last year.
Q. How many district delegates participated?
A. About 70 delegates from various districts in North China, South China and the Yangtsze Valley.
Q. How was the All-China National Salvation Association formed?
A. It had an Executive Committee of 41 members who, however, had not yet been appointed at that time. The Executive Committee in turn appointed a Standing Committee.

A. They were drawn up at the general meeting by persons appointed to do the work.
Q. What was the manifesto of the general meeting for?
A. To explain to the Government and people our suggestions for resisting the foe.
Q. What were the general political principles intended for?
A. They were intended to solicit preliminary views of the various parties.
Q. What did they mean by "allying with various Parties and cliques?"
A. They did not point to any definite party. The various Parties and cliques throughout the country all hoped to join hands together to resist Japan.
Q. Was the Kuomintang included?
A. The Kuomintang was naturally included; in fact it occupied the leading position.
Q. Did it mean a government to be jointly organized by the various Parties and cliques?
A. Nothing of the sort was said and furthermore such a government was not needed in view of the fact that there is already the National Government.
Q. The general political principles advocated a general election and the convention of a National Congress. What did this mean?
A. This was based on the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen's declaration to convene a National Congress when he went to North China.
Q. The general political principles advocated the establishment of a united political regime in the country after the convention of the National Congress. What did this mean?

3
June 12, 1937. Morning Translation.

A. This meant that national unification would strengthen
the government's power to resist Japan.
Q. Did the "allying with various Parties and cliques" mean
the toleration of Communism?
A. According to the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen's instructions,
the toleration of Communism is a good thing for the
consolidation of strength, but since the purge among
the communists this toleration has been condemned.
All the documents of the national salvation association
only advocate the cessation of civil wars, but have
never mentioned toleration of communism.
Q. Do you favour Communism?
A. The national salvation association did not speak of
principles. If there were any, they were simply those
of resistance to Japan and saving of the nation.
Q. National salvation and resistance against Japan is a
communistic slogan, is it not?
A. Communists eat rice and we also eat rice. Cannot we
resist Japan?
Q. Do you know that the communists on one hand advocate
resistance against Japan while on the other they suggest
revolution?
A. I do not know; this question must be put to the communists.
Q. Were there any communists in the national salvation
association?
A. We had no knowledge of this as we only paid attention
to the anti-Japanese question.
Q. When did you issue the booklet together with Tsang Nai-
chi, Tseu Tao-fun and Dao Ying-ts (陶行知)?
A. Probably in July.
Q. Can you remember the contents of the booklet?
A. The main object of this booklet was to call for
consolidation against insults.
Q. Why did you all issue the booklet?
A. The work for the salvation of the nation is extraordinarily
difficult and it is not easy for the public to understand
it. For this reason, we issued the booklet.
Q. Do you all object to the campaign of the Government to
suppress the communists?
A. We only opposed the Sino-Japanese co-operation against
the communists and we did not mention the subject
regarding the suppression of the communists. Nevertheless,
we paid close attention to the fact that the Government
had been engaged in the communist suppression campaign
for a period of ten years and that the people were in
much distress.
Q. What expression had the Communist Party made towards
the issue of offering resistance against Japan?
A. I learned from the newspapers that the communists desired
to pass through Shansi to resist Japan.
Q. Had you all any connection with the Communist Party?
A. We never had any connection with the Communist Party.
This may be verified by the letter from Mau Shih-tung
(毛泽东), stating that he had read our suggestions in
the newspapers.

4
June 12, 1937. Morning Translation

Q. When was the circular telegram addressed to Chang Hsueh-liang sent?
A. It was issued probably in November and this telegram was not addressed particularly to Chang Hsueh-liang alone. In the meantime, a circular telegram was issued addressed to the National Government, General Fu Tso-nyi, General Han Fu-chu, General Sung Cheh-yuen and other military leaders requesting them to assist Suiyuan.
Q. Was the National Salvation Association registered with the authorities?
A. The National Salvation Association was entirely open to the public and was unregistered.
Q. Did you know about the Sian Revolt?
A. I was in the detention house at that time and did not know of it.
Q. Did you read the resolutions passed by the Third Internationale?
A. I knew them after reading the prosecution against us.
Q. In which year was the 7th Conference of the Third Internationale held?
A. This should be referred to the Communist Party as I have no knowledge of this.
Q. Did you have any connection with the strikes in Shanghai?
A. I was not a worker and am ignorant. Please mention to which strike you refer.
Q. I refer to the strike declared on December 13, 1935 in the Japanese cotton mills.
A. I knew of the strike only after I read the newspapers.
Q. Was the Strike Support Committee formed by you all.
A. No. At the meeting in celebration of the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, the workers asked for support. A sum of some $400 was collected in subscriptions during the meeting.
Q. What is the difference between the People's Front and the National Salvation Joint Front?
A. We never used the expression: People's Front.
Q. Did you all secretly send Loo Tsing to form the Kiangsu National Salvation Association?
A. No.
Q. Have you any more to say?
A. I am very puzzled as to why the responsibility for the Sian Incident is foisted upon us. The Judge is requested to summon Chang Hsueh-liang to serve as a witness.

The lawyer defending Sung Chun-tz declared that no representatives from Sian attended the meetings of the All China National Salvation Association and that this will be seen from a perusal of the Intelligence Report for Averting of National Extinction (救亡情报) and also the minutes of these meetings.

Tsang Nai-chi's Statement

Tsang Nai-chi was next interrogated by the Judge as follows :-
Q. Did you know Loo Tsing?
A. He came to find me on the day before my arrest.

5
June 12, 1937. Morning Translation.

Q: What did you give him?
A: I gave him the manifesto and general principles of the National Salvation Association and the booklet.
Q. Was it you who gave him the mimeographed letter of Mau Shih-tung and the open letter addressed to the Kuomintang by the Communist Party?
A. No.
Q. Did Lo Ching join the National Salvation Association?
A. No. He would have been welcome if he had desired to join.
Q. Was it you who sent him out to undertake national salvation work?
A. The work of the National Salvation Association was all carried out at one's own initiative. Never was anyone sent out to undertake such work.
(For other replies of the accused to questions asked by the Court, see the statement of Sung Chun-dz.)
The following points were then raised by the lawyers acting in the defence of this accused:-
(1) The manifesto issued by the Third Plenary Session; the resolution passed by this Session in connection with the suppression of the Red menace; the statement issued by General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan, after the conclusion of this Session; and the manifesto issued by the National Crisis Conference held in April of the 21st Year (1932) of the Chinese Republic; the Court was requested to investigate as to whether or not all this is inconsistent with the proposals of the National Salvation Association.
(2) The second conference of the Executive Members of the National Salvation Association was held at the home of Mr. Ma Siang-pah. The Court was requested to enquire from Mr. Ma of the resolutions of this meeting.
(3) The Court was also requested to find out from the National Government and Generals Sung Cheh-yuan, Han Fu-chu and Fu Tso-nyi as to whether or not the telegrams they received from the National Salvation Association were identical to that addressed to General Chang Hsueh-liang.

Wong Zao-dz's Statement

The following questions were then put to accused Wong Zao-dz:-
Q. There appeared in the manifesto of the National Salvation Association an expression advocating the establishment of a political power for resistance against Japan. Does not this expression mean the overthrow of the present Government?
A. What I have studied is politics. I, therefore, only understand that "Government" is different from "Political Powers". What we have proposed is the strengthening of the political power of the Government; we did not demand a reorganization of the Government.
Q. Then do you agree to the system wherein the political power is monopolized in the hands of one "Party"?
A. So far as I am concerned, I have no objections, as I am one who favours the Constitution.

June 12, 1937.
6
Morning Translation.

Li Kung-poh's Statement

The 4th accused brought forward for interrogation was Li Kung-poh. The questions put to him were generally the same as those to the previous accused. Briefly, his statement is as follows: "The All-China National Salvation Association was inaugurated at the end of May or thereabouts last year. At that time I was not in Shanghai, so I did not participate in the inauguration of the Association. The manifesto and the 'General Principles on Politics' issued by the Association were known to me only after the inauguration meeting of the Association. The object of the manifesto and the General Principles is to bring about the concentration of the united efforts of the people throughout the country for resistance against Japan under the guidance of the Central Government. The term 'Political Power' refers to the 'strength of the political administration of the Government.' So far as the National Salvation Association is concerned, it has no political ambition whatever. Its efforts were to work for the unification of all Parties and cliques with the Government. I am entirely ignorant of the circumstances of the Sian Incident. It is true that a telegram was sent to General Chang Hsueh-liang, but it advocated resistance against Japan. Moreover, telegrams were addressed to various military leaders of this country, requesting them to pledge their unanimous support in the defence of Suiyuan Province."

Here the lawyers acting in the defence of this accused pointed out that the circumstances of the strike of the workers of the Japanese cotton mills in Shanghai were known to the authorities. The Court was requested to investigate as to whether or not this strike had had any affiliations with the National Salvation Association.

Tseu Tao-fun's Statement

The following questions were put to accused Tseu Tao-fun:-
Q. Did you take part in the inauguration meeting of the All-China National Salvation Association?
A. As I was then in Hongkong, I did not participate in the meeting. It was only after I had been notified after my return to Shanghai in July that I knew that I had been elected as a member of the Executive Committee of the Association.
Q. Do you agree with the contents of the manifesto issued by the Association?
A. Yes, I do.
Q. There appeared in the booklet expressions about "a meeting for aversion of national extinction". What does this mean?
A. It means to bring about the concentration of all the talents of the country to deal with Japan.
Q. What is the difference between "The People's Front" and "The National Salvation Front"?
A. The object of the "People's Front" is to oppose Fascism, while that of "The National Salvation Front" is not; it advocates united resistance against Japan, the recovery of the Four North-Eastern Provinces and the restoration of our sovereign rights in North China.

7
June 12, 1937. Morning Translation

Here the lawyers acting in the defence of this accused pointed out that the proposals and views of the accused could be obtained from all his writings. The Court was requested to investigate as to whether or not his proposals are irreconcilable with the Three Principles of the People.

Next interrogated was Sz Liang who made the following statement :-
"I was one of the Standing Committee members of the All-China National Salvation Association as well as of the Women's National Salvation Association. The motive in issuing a manifesto and drafting a set of general principles on politics by the Association was to effect the concentration of the strength of the people throughout the country and to unite together all people, irrespective of sex or class. The proposal that all parties and cliques which are different in views should unite together was not aimed at seizing the political power of the National Government because we had absolutely no idea of re-organizing the Government. We do not mean that the Constitution set up by the Government is useless, because at this time when a national crisis confronts the country, the salvation of the nation is the most important task before our people; the question of the Constitution should be left over for consideration. Furthermore, the aim of our Association is to save the nation. We have never talked about the People's Front. The characters 'national salvation front' mean that all Chinese people should stand on the same front to save the nation."

Soo Chi-li who was then interrogated made the following statement :-
"The main object in proposing the unity of all parties and cliques is to effect resistance against Japan. All people who belong to the Chinese race should therefore unite together. As regards the question of the Constitution, we have only made comments upon it, and as a rule, people are allowed to make comments over their dissatisfaction. It does not necessarily follow that we have protested against the Constitution. We have never talked about communism because at this time when we have no time to lose in the task for the salvation of the nation, it is impossible for us to make a study of communism. The Sian Revolt came to our knowledge only at the time of our interrogation by the Procurator."

Finally, Loo Tsing was interrogated, and he made the following statement :-
"The formation of the Kiangsu National Salvation Association was on my own initiative, not on the instructions of Tsang Nai-chi. At this time when the fate of the nation is at stake, all Chinese people, if not traitors, should rise and unite together to take up the work of salvation of the nation and resistance against Japan."

The other accused such as Koo Liu-ching and Ning Zoong-kao stated that they had no connection with the Association.

June 12, 1937.

Sung Chun-dz was in fine spirits, while Tseu
Tao-fun made the following remarks to certain persons

movement. I will not do anything against my conscience."

Ta Kung Pao (Editorial) :-

Sung Chun-dz and six others have been charged for injuring the Republic of China.

The national crisis reached its climax last year and the people were excited. As the Government could not make public all the steps taken in dealing with the situation, many people were dissatisfied. Following the victory in Suiyuan and the Sian Incident, the attitude of the Government became known among the people who then began to trust the work of consolidation of the Government instead of suspecting it as before.

Prior to the latter part of last year, the youths in the country usually welcomed anti-Government and anti-Kuomintang comments. However, they have now changed their attitude by favouring a strong unification of the country. Members of the so-called National Salvation Federation favoured quick action to deal with external affairs and really their policy was erroneous in many ways. As a matter of fact, their background was formed by the radical ideas of the people. Although we cannot surmise what changes have taken place in people's minds during the past six months, yet at least the minds of those who were formerly in sympathy with the National Salvation Federation have undergone certain changes through the Suiyuan fighting and the Sian Incident.

We are of the opinion that if the authorities insist on charges against them for their past action, it might cause uneasiness among the people, especially at the present time when the Government is working for the consolidation of the minds of the people. We hope that the Judges concerned will pay attention to this point.

Ying-ts (陶行知), Loo Tsing (羅青), Koo Lieu-shing (顧留馨),
Zung Zoong-kao (任仲言), Chang Zoong-me (張仲勉), Chen
Dao-hung (陳道宏) and Chen Tso (陳卓) are being charged
with offences against the internal security of the State.
    It is said that the reason the Soochow High
Court has charged the latter seven persons is as follows:-
    Dao Ying-ts is an educationalist and he has
never been summoned by the High Court at Soochow in connection
with the case.    He is now teaching in America.    An order
for his arrest has been issued.
    Loo Tsing, who was formerly a secretary with
the Tseng-Tai Railway Administration, was arrested one
year ago.    He is still being detained at Soochow.
    Koo Lieu-shing, Zung Zoong-kao, Chang Zoong-me,
Chen Dao-hung and Chen Tso are members of the National
Salvation Federation of Various Public Bodies in Shanghai.
In January, they, in company with 16 others, proceeded to
Soochow and requested the High Court to release Sung Chun-
dz and six others.    In February they received summonses
instructing them to appear at the Court.    Koo and Zung
appeared at the Court on February 3 and were detained until
the 10th when they were bailed out.
    The names of the latter seven persons are also
included in the charge filed by the Soochow High Court.
Furthermore, the Court has issued orders for their arrest.
    The charge is very lengthy and contains the
following points: "The accused, with intent to injure the
Republic of China, have formed organizations which propagate
doctrines against the Three Principles of the People.    In
accordance with Article 11 and 28 of the Criminal Code,
they have committed crimes mentioned in Article 6 of the
Law Governing the Punishment of Persons Who Commit Acts
with Intent to Injure the Republic of China.    In addition
to issuing orders for the arrest of Dao Ying-ts, Chang
Zoong-me, Chen Dao-hung and Chen Tso whose whereabouts
are not known, this Court is now charging all of them under
Articles 230 and 243 of the Code of Criminal Procedure".
    Article 6 of the Law Governing the Punishment of
Persons Who Commit Acts with Intent to Injure the Republic
of China states: "Whosoever with intent to injure the
Republic of China organizes associations, holds meetings,
or propagates a doctrine irreconcilable with the Three principles
of the People shall be punished with imprisonment
for not less than five years, and not more than fifteen
years".    The families of the accused are prepared to retain
three lawyers each for the defence.    The Soochow Bar
Association has appointed five lawyers to defend the accused.
    It is learned that the Soochow High Court will
hear the case sometime this week.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

GENERAL CHANG CHUN ON SINO-JAPANESE RELATIONS

General Chang Chun, the former Minister
of Foreign Affairs, now Secretary-General of the Central
Political Council and Chairman of the Diplomatic Affairs
Committee, came to Shanghai the other day to undergo
treatment to his nose.
When interviewed yesterday at his residence
by a reporter of this paper, General Chang Chun made the
following statement:- "I accepted the post of Minister of
Foreign Affairs last year on condition that I served for
six months only. As regards negotiations for the
readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations, the attitude of
the Chinese Government has already been made quite clear
to Japan in the course of my conferences with Mr. Kawagoe,

will be no necessity to solve the Sino-Japanese disputes
separately or partially. The recent speech delivered by
the Japanese Minister of Foreign Affairs represented what
I would have liked to say. A solution of all outstanding
Sino-Japanese disputes will depend upon Japan's sincerity."

Shanghai Public Daily News ( 市公日刊 ) publishes the following brief comment :-

THE POLICE AND HAWKERS

It is proper that those hawkers who in peddling their wares, create obstruction to traffic or who pay no heed to sanitation should be suppressed. But on reflection, one sees that these hawkers are being compelled to do such a low class of business because they have no other means to earn a living.
One regrettable fact is that the authorities of the Foreign Settlements have no fixed measures by which to handle these hawkers. They arrest the hawkers but release them soon afterwards when the hawkers have paid a fine. Furthermore, there are certain Police officers who regard hawkers as "meat and fish" and squeeze and extortion have become common.
The Chinese Ratepayers' Association is taking up the case of the hawkers. We hope that the Settlement authorities will not be too harsh towards hawkers at this time of trade depression and will instruct Police officers not to take advantage of their authority to oppress hawkers.

THE LAW OF CONNIVANCE IN ADULTERY

The Judicial Yuan has given the following
explanation of the text of Article 245, Section 2, of the
Chinese Criminal Code :-
No private complaint can be made when the
spouse has connived at the other party's adultery with
another person, and such right of private complaint can
not be exercised should the spouse later repent. Connivance
means the act of the spouse in allowing the other party to
commit the offence, the consent of the spouse to the adultery
with the third party not being in question.

The Eastern Daily News ( 东方时报 ) :-
RISE IN THE VALUE OF COPPERS
Of late, the exchange value of coppers has taken a sharp rise. For one dollar, only 293 coppers are given in exchange, while a 10-cent note is worth only 29 coppers. The takings of the tramway companies, whose main source of income is in coppers, are now mostly in paper money. For this reason there is a shortage of coppers on the market. This is one of the causes for the sharp rise in the value of coppers.
It is also said that many traitorous Kompo merchants are collecting and smuggling out large quantities of coppers for a certain nation, because they can be used as material in the manufacture of arms and ammunition.
Some two weeks ago, three Kompo men were arrested by the West Gate Branch Bureau of Police and several hundred thousands of coppers were seized. In Hongkew, the collecting of coppers for export to a certain country is more active. This is really the principal cause for the rise in the exchange value of coppers. It is to be hoped that the authorities will devise ways and means to put a stop to this practice so as to avert a panic in financial circles.

The Ching Zung ( 錦章 ) Silk Weaving Factory on Brenan Road employs about 30 workers.
Recently the management ordered that the length of silk to be woven by each worker is to be increased by one-third. As this would mean a big loss of wage to them, the workers appointed representatives to open negotiations with the management, but without result.
The management then ordered the caterer to stop supplying meals. Upon learning of this, the workers suspended operations.
The local Tangpu and other government organs will mediate.

According to the executioner, the rope
was tested on the previous evening and was found to be
quite strong and in good order. How the rope came to give
way is unknown. In our opinion, it may have been due
to the heavy weight of the man.
A difficulty now arises: according to
British law, there can be only one execution of the
sentence imposed upon a prisoner. Whether the prisoner
Ab Singh, after recovering from his injury, will have
to undergo another process of hanging or whether he will
be exempted from further punishment is a legal question.
If he be exempted from further punishment, then, from the
legal point of view, he has got off lightly, especially
in view of the fact that the prisoner had been convicted
of murder; but if he has to undergo another process of
hanging, then from a humanitarian point of view, it would
be rather cruel to make him suffer mentally and physically
a second time.

be abolished. When a man has committed a crime deserving
a death penalty, he should be executed painlessly and
with dispatch.

Ta Kung Pao publishes the following article contributed by
one Chin Wen (秋文) :-

A FOOL BEGGAR

"Give me a copper".
I used to hear this remark when I was eating
in a restaurant. He is a middle aged man.
(A beggar approaches) "Fool beggar! Let
us hear you speak a foreign language!" said a child aged
about 12 years, who is the offspring of the shop owner.
"Can he speak a foreign language?", asked
a man who was in the shop waiting for some refreshment.
"Yes", replied the female owner. "He was
formerly a cook in the employ of foreigners and can speak
a foreign language. If he was not such a fool, he would
not have become a beggar".
Another man asked, "How did he become stupid?"
In reply, the female owner said, "He was
frightened by a foreigner and went mad. The foreigner
lost his temper because he had made a mistake when he
cooked a meal. The foreigner drew his pistol and pointing
it at him, said that he would shoot him down. The man
became excited and thus became stupid. The foreigner
did not want his services and he is now begging".
In the past, I hated the slave "boys" in
the employ of foreigners. Now I understand that their
slavish behaviour is due to oppression on the part of
"foreign gentlemen". It shows the viciousness and
violence of the foreigners.

Chin Pao (今报) :-

THE ARREST OF MR. SUNG CHUN DZ AND OTHERS

Messrs. Sung Chun Dz (沈鈞儒), Tseu Tao
Feng (鄒奮), Tsang Nai Chi (章乃器), Wong Zau Dz
(王造時), So Tsien Li (沙千里) and Li Kung Pch (李公樸)
are being detained in the new detention house of the High
Court at Soochow. They are allowed to read books sent them
by friends etc., but the books must first be examined and
approved of by the Procurator. They are not permitted to
read newspapers as they are considered too "stimulative".
It is evident that the prisoners are under a more strict
control as compared to the control exercised when they were
detained by the Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety.
Visitors are carefully questioned by the
Procurator regarding their names, nativities, occupations,
relations with the prisoners and reasons for the visits.
Persons who are making a second visit have to go through the
same questioning. This is being done deliberately in order
to deter friends and relations from visiting the prisoners.
However, there are still more than ten visitors each day.
The prisoners have been arraigned before
the Investigation Court on three separate occasions, but
no public trial has been held up to the present. The Judge
appears to adopt a favourable attitude towards the prisoners,
but it is hard to predict what will be the result of the
case.

LAI ICHI:

R.D ORDER ARRESTED

Since the outbreak of the strikes in local
Japanese cotton mills, Yangtszepoo Police Station has been
making every effort to trace the instigators of the strikes.
Through the efforts of officers of this Station and of the
Special Branch, S.M.P., it was learned that the various
National Salvation Associations connected with the Communist
Party have been very active behind these strikers.
A male Chinese worker named Tuan Chi Ling (段奇林)
was arrested by Detective Sergeant Ueoka of Yangtszepoo
Police Station at the Shanghai Spinning and Weaving Company.
This man who is a communist is reported to have acted as
a medium of communication between the instigators and the
strikers. When his house was searched by Police, a quantity
of literature relating to the strikes was discovered.
He was charged in the First Special District Court at 9 a.m.
November 24 and was remanded for one week.
Although a close investigation was made by the
Special Branch, S.M.P., regarding a Chinese female
teacher who was arrested outside the Dong Shing Cotton
Mill, she was released by the Court for lack of evidence.

Tung Nan Wan Pao published the following article, contributed
by one Yea Ting ( 叶挺 ), on December 15:-

NO CHINESE IS WILLING TO BE A SLAVE

No Chinese is willing to be a slave. This is
demonstrated by the bravery exhibited by our soldiers at
the front and the surrender of large numbers of bandit
troops who, only a few days ago, were fighting stubbornly
against our soldiers.
Really these bandit troops are not to blame,
for it is their leaders such as Prince Teh, Li Shou Shin,
Wong Ying, who are the real traitors. At first the bandit
troops did not know that in fighting the Government forces
they were creating opportunities for Japan to oppress China
and acting as Japan's running dogs. But now that they have
realized their mistake they are surrendering in large numbers.
It is our hope that the other bandit troops
who have not yet surrendered will follow the example of
those who have surrendered and help to kill those heartless
traitors and the ambitious Japanese militarists.
Let us not shed each other's blood, let us
shed the blood of the Japanese. Let all Chinese stand in
a united front against our enemy and refuse to be slaves!

Ta Kung Pao publishes the following article :-

TWO PLAYS ENTITLED "MOTHER OF ABYSSINIA" AND "THE
HOME OF A WORKER"

In connection with the entertainment to be
given at the Chinese Y.W.C.A. the other day in aid of
the Suiyuan fund, the Dou Lin Dramatic Society (駝鈴劇社)

is of less value than a piece of toilet paper.

Lib Foo and other local newspapers :-

THE CASE OF MISS SZE LIANG

Yesterday morning the Procuratorate of
the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High Court instructed the
Procurator of the Shanghai Second Special District Court
to summon lawyers Tung Hwa (唐豪) and Chang Tse Liang
(張之讓) for interrogation as to the whereabouts of Miss
Sze Liang (史良).

When questioned by Chief Prosecutor
Sung Lau Kong (孫瀏康) as to whether or not Miss Sze
Liang would appear that day (December 12), lawyer Chang
Tse Liang stated: "Sometime ago, I sent a telegram to lawyer
Tung Hwa (唐豪) in Peiping enquiring into the whereabouts
of Miss Sze Liang and received a reply from Mr. Tung stating
that he did not know. On December 10 I received a letter
from Miss Sze Liang addressed from No. 80 Kuan Chien Ka
(觀前街), Soochow, stating that after she was released
on bail, she at once proceeded to her native place to look
after her grandmother who was then ill and that her failure
to appear at Court afterwards was due to an attack of
vomiting of blood. I therefore request the Court to time
postpone the hearing of the case for one week by which Miss
Sze Liang will be able to present herself in Court."

The Procurator said that Miss Sze Liang
should appear and that it would be better for her to appear
at the earliest possible date before the Kiangsu High Court
at Soochow and that this Court would not trouble her if
she presented herself first at that Court.

The two lawyers who are acting as
guarantors of Miss Sze Liang promised to publish an
advertisement calling upon Miss Sze Liang to put in an
appearance.

The Procurator then remanded the case
for further hearing on December 19.

According to enquiries made by our
representative at Soochow, the place from which the letter
of Miss Sze Liang was sent was formerly occupied by the
Sung Dah Loong Brass Work Shop but has since been converted
into a garage by the China South Seas Bank. It is at present
unoccupied.

The Political Section of the French
Municipal Police details three detectives every to keep
a watch at the home of Miss Sze Liang in Shanghai.

National Herald:-

MEETING OF RICKSHA COOLIES

On December 10 the Special District Ricksha
coolies held a meeting in their office at Zia Jao (斜桥).
Seventy-five representatives of ricksha coolies from five
districts were present.
Tung D. Sung (陳濤生), who presided, made
a report on the petitions sent to the S.M.C. for the
reorganization of the Pullers Mutual Aid Association.
The following resolutions were passed:-
(1) That the S.M.C. be warned to dismiss Mr. Chang Tung
Ying (張登瀛), Chief Secretary of the P.M.A.A., as
soon as possible.
(2) The S.M.C. has resolved to abolish the contributions to
the P.M.A.A., and to increase the license fee.
Resolved: That, as ricksha coolies will still be
the actual payers of the contributions, the contributions
should be known as coolies' contributions to the P.M.A.A.
as before.
(3) That representatives be sent to Nanking to ask the
National Government to order the Shanghai City Government
to organize ricksha coolies' relief undertakings, to
adopt a unified control of the ricksha business and to take
over the Ricksha Board and the P.M.A.A. so as to uphold
the rights of the country.

December , 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Chen (新人), a weekly magazine, published the following article on December 5 :-

THE ARREST OF MR. SUNG CHUN SHIH AND OTHERS : THEIR ACTIVITIES CONDEMNED

The Shanghai City Government on November 26 published in newspapers a statement on the arrest of Messrs Sung Chun Shih (沈儒), Li Kung Pu (李公樸), Won Chao Shih (王造時), Chang Nan Chi (章乃器), Chow Tao Feng (鄒韜奮) and Soo Chi Lien (沙千里), in which it states that they were being charged with plotting disturbances of the peace and order and attempting to overthrow the National Government. As such activities are unlawful, they are to be dealt with according to law.

We know that Mr. Li Kung Pu is the publisher of the "Intelligence" (情報生活) and Mr. Chow Tao Feng is the publisher of the "Livelihood Weekly" (生活星期刊).

From the contents of these two periodicals, one can see that these six men used frequently to publish comments promoting a "people's front" and a "united front". They were carrying out their objects in the name of national salvation.

It is clear that the "people's front" supported by Messrs Sung Chun Shih and the others is against the Government. They hold the opinion that it is the people who should resist the enemy. For this reason, the people's front must unite to overthrow the Government to pave the way to resistance to the enemy and the salvation of the country.

The "united front" is directed against the Kuomintang because they hold the view that the Kuomintang is not in a position to advocate resistance to the enemy and the salvation of the nation, therefore the Communist Party, the Social Democratic Party and all other cliques should form a united front to promote resistance to the enemy. Their shouts of resistance to the enemy and salvation of the nation have misled the people into believing that these are the only ways to save the country. Thus their activities are harmful to the country.

The six men have been arrested, but their followers are continuing to publish comments that are injurious to the country. The Government should suppress them as well as annihilate the movement altogether.

Ta Kung Pao (Editorial) :-

    Mr. Sung Chun Shih and five others are at
present in the custody of the Shanghai Bureau of Public
Safety.    We have refrained from commenting on this case
because no particulars are known, furthermore, the case is
sub judice.
    (1) Mr. Sung Chun Shih and the others are all
well known writers in Shanghai.    Their case has attracted
much attention among cultural circles.    Every Chinese
citizen should observe the law and any person who is
suspected of a crime will incur the penalty of the law,
but this must be carried out according to legal procedure.
This should be strictly observed, particularly in cases to
which the community is paying much attention.    When the
authorities made the arrests, they must have a suspicion
that the six persons had committed some offence.    In that
event, why have they not been referred to Court to be dealt
with instead of being detained at the Bureau for so many
days already?    According to law, the Police must arraign
an arrested man before a Court within 24 hours.    Why has
this procedure not been observed in the present case?
    (2) The six persons are writers or social
conditions.    Their speeches and activities have a certain
effect among a section of the community.    So far as we
know, the body which these six persons organized this year
has not been registered with the authorities.    In the view
of the authorities, this is an offence.    The authorities
had not interfered with their activities in the past because
they did not suspect their motives.
    Now, this case happened at a time when the
Government is leading the country in national salvation
work.    According to a brief communique issued by the local
authorities, new developments in the case seem to have
taken place.    If this is true, the case should be
immediately referred to the Court for investigation and
a charge can be filed so that the truth might be revealed.
These men should be immediately restored to freedom if the
Court, after holding an inquiry, decides against a
prosecution.
    (3) We hope the Government will be lenient
to these men.    If a person is simply under a suspicion
which can be explained away or if the matter arose through
a misunderstanding, he should be allowed to argue his case.
If the facts in the present case admit of such
explanation or pleading, the Court should rule that no
prosecution should be instituted.    We think this step is
desirable because we are of the opinion that, in order to
save the country, it is important that the country be free
of internal troubles, and to accomplish this there must be
sincerity and good will between the Government and the
people.    This sincerity and good will should first be
shown by the Government.
    The China of the past, or even the China
of six months ago, cannot be compared with the China of
to-day, for China is now a united country.    In fact, our
Government is at this very moment directing the whole
country in the struggle against alien aggression.    To

save the country, every bit of national power, visible and

THE ARREST OF MR. SUNG CHUN SHIH AND OTHERS : THEIR ACTIVITIES CONDEMNED

Ta Kung Pao (Editorial) :-

Mr. Sung Chun Shih and five others are at
present in the custody of the Shanghai Bureau of Public
Safety. We have refrained from commenting on this case
because no particulars are known, furthermore, the case is
sub judice.
(1) Mr. Sung Chun Shih and the others are all
well known writers in Shanghai. Their case has attracted
much attention among cultural circles. Every Chinese
citizen should observe the law and any person who is
suspected of a crime will incur the penalty of the law,
but this must be carried out according to legal procedure.
This should be strictly observed, particularly in cases to
which the community is paying much attention. When the
authorities made the arrests, they must have a suspicion
that the six persons had committed some offence. In that
event, why have they not been referred to Court to be dealt
with instead of being detained at the Bureau for so many
days already? According to law, the Police must arraign
an arrested man before a Court within 24 hours. Why has
this procedure not been observed in the present case?
(2) The six persons are writers on social
conditions. Their speeches and activities have a certain
effect among a section of the community. So far as we
know, the body which these six persons organized this year
has not been registered with the authorities. In the view
of the authorities, this is an offence. The authorities
had not interfered with their activities in the past because
they did not suspect their motives.
Now, this case happened at a time when the
Government is leading the country in national salvation
work. According to a brief communique issued by the local
authorities, new developments in the case seem to have
taken place. If this is true, the case should be
immediately referred to the Court for investigation and
a charge can be filed so that the truth might be revealed.
These men should be immediately restored to freedom if the
Court, after holding an inquiry, decides against a
prosecution.
(3) We hope the Government will be lenient
to these men. If a person is simply under a suspicion
which can be explained away or if the matter arose through
a misunderstanding, he should be allowed to argue his case.
If the facts in the present case admit of such
explanation or pleading, the Court should rule that no
prosecution should be instituted. We think this step is
desirable because we are of the opinion that, in order to
save the country, it is important that the country be free
of internal troubles, and to accomplish this there must be
sincerity and good will between the Government and the
people. This sincerity and good will should first be
shown by the Government.
The China of the past, or even the China
of six months ago, cannot be compared with the China of
to-day, for China is now a united country. In fact, our
Government is at this very moment directing the whole
country in the struggle against alien aggression. To

Morning Translation.

save the country, every bit of national power, visible and invisible, should be put together to make a united power. We must bear in mind that the power possessed by a section of the literary class can be used as a part of national power if properly utilized.
(4) We wish also to make a few remarks to members of literary circles. All persons engaged in the national salvation movement should make their organization and activities conform to law. This is particularly important at the present moment. In plain words, apart from upholding the Government, all other activities are quite unnecessary. Organizations of the people are necessary only when the political situation is in a state of confusion and the Government has become powerless. But such is not the case in China to-day. While it must be admitted that a great deal of reconstruction work and improvement has yet to be accomplished in political and financial matters, we must not overlook the great improvements that have already been achieved during the past six months. At a time when a new situation has arisen, it is the duty of patriotic persons to place their trust in the Government and not to confuse the situation by their acts. We trust the literary circles will recognize this. Mistaken notions should be corrected immediately. As to liberty of speech, we are confident that it will be permitted by the Government so long as military secrets are not divulged.

PRO-SOVIET CHINESE PARTY ACTIVELY WORKING TO

Six Chinese named Sung Chun

Nan Chi, and Chow Tao Feng, important officers of the
Chinese National Salvation Association, who were arrested
for reactionary activities, are still being detained at

Associations have started a movement among anti-Japanese

engaged in securing signatures. The work will take at
least a month.

Co-operative Agreement has caused consternation among the
members of the Chinese Pro-Soviet Party. They are
reported to have approached the Nanking Government to
conclude a Sino-Soviet Co-operative Agreement with a view
to opposing Japan. Consequently, they will assist the
activities of the National Salvation Associations.

of the Soviet Government is endeavouring to secure
co-operation between Soviet officers in Shanghai and

November 28, 1936. Morning Translation.

T Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

MESSRS CHANG NAN CHI AND CHOW T.O FENG HANDED OVER TO
SHANGHAI DISTRICT COURT

Miss Sze Liang (史良), a lawyer residing
in the French Concession, Mr. Chang Nan Chi (章乃器), an
economist, and Mr. Chow Tao Feng (周韬奋), publisher of
the "Livelihood Weekly" (生活周刊), were arrested during
the night of November 22/23 by the Public Safety Bureau
with the assistance of the French Police on a charge of
inciting labour unrest. On November 23, they were arraigned
before the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court and
were allowed bail.
On November 24, only Messrs Chang and Chow
appeared in the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court.
Miss Sze failed to attend. The Court ordered them to
be detained.
On November 25, Messrs Chang and Chow were
again brought before the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High
Court. An order was issued that the case be investigated
by the Procurator of the Court. In the meantime, the
Court ordered the lawyers defending Miss Sze Liang to
produce her in Court.
After she was bailed out, Miss Sze Liang
left Shanghai on the following morning. Up to 5 p.m.
yesterday, she had still failed to appear in Court.
The French Police has detailed officers to her residence
and to railway stations and wharves in an endeavour to
effect her arrest.
Holding the view that both Messrs Chang Nan
Chi and Chow Tao Feng had committed acts that are harmful
to peace and order, the Shanghai District Court on November
27 sent Procurator Wong Chia Mei (王家楣) to the Third
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court to request their
extradition.
At 5.45 p.m. yesterday, Presiding Judge Wu
Ting Chi (吴廷祺), Judges Wong (王) and Liao (廖) and
Procurator Tung (董) held a hearing of their case in the
Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court. Mr. Yuen Chia Wang
(袁家望), the Municipal Advocate, the lawyers for the
defence, and Procurator Wong of the Shanghai District Court
were present.
Presiding Judge Wu ordered that Messrs Chang
Nan Chi and Chow Tao Feng be handed over to the Shanghai
District Court.
So far, Miss Sze Liang, a lawyer, has failed
to appear. Detectives from the Chinese and Foreign Police
have been sent to Soochow to locate and arrest her. It
is believed that she has gone to the North. More detectives
and policemen have been detailed to keep a watch at the
wharves and railway stations.
Our reporter made enquiries at the residence
of Miss Sze Liang in Lafayette Terrace, French Concession.
Her mother declared :- "The members of her family are
very much anxious over the whereabouts of Miss Sze Liang.
We do not know when she will return to Shanghai. Neither
her relatives nor her intimate friends know where she has
gone. She has a case for hearing at 9 a.m. November 26.
She may return before noon that day".

Society Evening News dated November 26 (comment) :-

ARREST OF MR. SUNG CHUN SHIH AND OTHERS

Messrs. Sung Chun Shih (沙鈞儒), Li
Kung Pu (李公樸), Wang Chao Shih (王造時), Chang
Nan Chi (章乃器), Chow Tao Feng (鄒奮) and Soo Chi
Lien (沙千里) and Miss Sze Liang (史良) were
recently arrested "on suspicion of instigating strikes."
These seven learned scholars are the leaders of the
national salvation movement and their arrest came as a
shock to us, especially in view of the fact that victories
are being gained in Suiyuan, a strong attitude is being
adopted in dealing with foreign affairs and the moment
seems opportune for the establishment of a popular front.
Messrs. Sung, Wang and Soo and Miss Sze
are well known lawyers and as such they have acted as
protectors of the people's rights. Inspired by a
spirit of righteousness, they have been undertaking
national salvation work. Their actions may have gone
beyond the limit, but we are confident that their motive
is proper.
Messrs. Li, Chow and Chang are respectively
the editors of such authoritative publications as the
"Livelihood" (生活), the "Intelligence" (讀書生活) etc.
Their articles have been well received by the public.
Their writings may appear to be inflammatory, but they
contained nothing that is malicious; they write what
every citizen of China wishes to say. They are not being
instigated by others. The spirit of nationalism that has
seized hold of the people at present is largely due to
their writings.
It is to be hoped that the authorities will
take these facts into consideration when dealing with these
three persons.
The authorities should conduct an
investigation into the case as soon as possible and release
the seven persons if there is no proof against them. The
arrest of these seven persons may please our enemy, but it
is distressing for us to witness such an event so soon
after the release from gaol of Mr. Doo Zung Yuen (杜重遠)
who was imprisoned in connection with the case of the
"New Life Weekly" (新生).

REPORTED ARREST OF MADAME SUN Y T SEN UNTRUE

"The Shanghai Mainichi", a local Japanese
newspaper, on November 26 published a report to the effect
that Madame Sun Yat Sen was arrested in the French
Concession on the morning of November 25 on a charge of
Communism.
On November 26, our reporter made enquiries
at Madame Sun's residence on Rue Moliere, French Concession
and learned that the report was absolutely groundless.

contrary to their hopes, such reports would result in a
consolidation of the country.

The Shanghai Public Daily News(市民日報) publishes the following leading article :-

THE ARREST OF LI KUNG FU AND OTHERS.

Between 2 and 3 a.m. on November 23, Messrs Li Kung Pu(李公樸), Wang Chao Shih(王造時), Soo Chi Lien(沙千里), Sung Chun Shih(沈鈞儒), Chow Tao Feng(韜奮), Chang Nan Chi(章乃器) and Miss Szo Liang(史良), seven patriotic leaders, were placed under arrest. The affair created a consternation among the public who were ignorant of the cause of this drastic action.

The following report was issued by the Central News Agency and published by the local newspapers yesterday :-

"Mr. Li Kung Pu and six others are being charged with operating illegal organizations, co-operating with communists, instigating strikes of workers and students and a general strike and other subversive activities with the object of overthrowing the Government. They were arrested by the authorities with the assistance of the Police of the Foreign Settlements on a charge of having committed offences against the internal security of the State."

We cannot help asking: "Have they really been arrested on such a charge?"

Nobody will excuse a person who betrays his nation under the cloak of patriotism. However, the seven persons under arrest are prominent leaders of the National Salvation Association and their thoughts, character and patriotism deserve sympathy and support. Moreover, they are all engaged in proper professions.

It has been said that there is a limit to patriotism; it is possible that their patriotism has been too fiery. Still, we cannot believe that any person who loves his country too strongly can be arrested and punished by the authorities. However, as the matter has been referred to the Courts, an explanation will be forthcoming.

MAINICHI AND OTHER LOCAL NEWSPAPERS :

TROUBLE BETWEEN KOREANS AND CHINESE

At about 1.10 p.m. November 24, a Korean
named Ken Nei-boku, 21, residing at No. 7 Yung Fu Li off
Woosung Road, visited another Korean named Kim Yu-toku,

November 25, 1936.    Morning Translation.

"At about 10 a.m. yesterday (November 19)
a pedestrian, an old man of more than 70 years of age,
was knocked down at the corner of Pingliang and Glen
Roads by a motor car (licence number unknown) which
was moving at a high speed. Upon finding that he had
caused an accident, the driver drove off at a high
speed. Later, a post duty policeman conveyed the
injured man to the Sacred Heart Hospital where the man
succumbed to his injuries soon after arrival."
It is known to everybody that there is a Police
Station at the corner of Pingliang and Glen Roads. Moreover,
the accident occurred opposite the Station. The place is
not an isolated locality. It is customary to have a
policeman on duty at the front gate of Police Station; the
accident happened at about 10 O'clock in the morning; yet
the motor car was driven off unnoticed after the accident.
I am of the opinion that an explanation should
be demanded from the Police authorities. We should not
overlook the matter just because the deceased was a poor
old man, for it is a case that concerns not only the
deceased but the general public as well.

November 24, 1936. Morning Translation.

Mr. Wang Chao Shih resides at No. 7
Tifeng Road. When our reporter called, only Mr. Wang's
mother and his six-year old son were at home. Mr. Wang
was arrested at 3 a.m. November 23. He offered no
objection to his arrest after he was shown an official
document by the three police officers who had come to
arrest him.

The home of Mr. Sung Chung Shih is
located at No. 51, Tao Yuen Villa (桃源村), Yuyuen Road.
When the five police officers called on the morning of
November 23, he was fast asleep. The officers were
admitted into the house by a servant. One of the officers
remained on guard outside the house, one in the hall, while
the other three followed the servant upstairs. Upon
learning of the arrest, the elder son of Mr. Sung Chung
Shih, who lives at house No. 53 in the same alleyway,
immediately called at his father's home. Both the father
and the son were shown the official despatch from the
Bureau of Public Safety. After a brief consultation with
his son, Mr. Sung Chung Shih left with the officers.

Mr. Li Kung Fu resides at No. 24 Han
Chong Li (亨昌里) off Yuyuen Road. When the police
officers arrived at 2 a.m. November 23, Mr. Li happened
to be out with friends. The officers remained in the
house until about 2.30 a.m. when Mr. Li returned and was
placed under arrest.

The residence of lawyer Soo Chi Lien is
situate at No. 14, Lane No. 524, Avenue Road. When the
police officers arrived, he was in bed.

Mr. Chang Nan Chi resides at No. 24
Shih Wei Li (施卫里) off Route Delastre, French Concession.
Officers of the French Police, accompanied by members of
the Bureau of Public Safety, arrived at the place at 2 a.m.
November 23. They climbed over a short bamboo fence
outside the front gate and were admitted into the house
by the inmates. They immediately proceeded upstairs and
showing Mr. Chang the official document, they placed him
under arrest.

Lawyer Sze Liang lives at No. 1 Lafayette
Villa, Rue Lafayette. At first the foreign and Chinese
detectives could not effect an entrance either from the
front or the back gate, because the inmates refused to
open the door for fear of robbers. The officers then
climbed over the short wall in front of the main gate and
effected an entry into the main hall from where they
immediately proceeded upstairs. Upon being shown
the official document, lawyer Sze Liang at once dressed
herself and left with the officers.

Mr. Chow Tao Feng lives at No. 1, Lane
No. 601, Rue Lafayette. The police officers were admitted
by himself. One of the members of the Bureau of Public
Safety then said to him: "I have been shadowing you for
three days and saw you returning home in a ricksha at about
11 p.m. November 22. I immediately notified the French
Police and we have now come to arrest you." The police
officers then seized several English books which they took
to the station for examination.

Kiangsu High Court at 9 a.m. November 23. The proceedings
were held in camera. Only Mr. King S. Kum, the Municipal
Advocate, the lawyers for the defence and the police officers
in charge of the case were present.
After a lengthy interrogation, Judge Nyi allowed
the accused to be released on bail furnished by their
respective lawyers. Messrs. Chang Yi Fan (張以藩),
Ngoh Goong (吳森) and Chen Tse Kao (陳志皋) are
appearing for Mr. Li Kung Pu; Messrs. Yu Chung Loh (俞鍾輅)
and Li Yung Chi (李文池) for Mr. Wang Chao Shih; Messrs.
Chang Yao Tseng (張耀曾) and Chen Tse Kao for Mr. Sung
Chun Shih; Messrs. Tsai Loh Zung (蔡天東), Yang Tien Sung
(楊天遜) and Aung Pao Chi (汪葆楫) for Mr. Soo Chi Lien.
All the guarantors were instructed to produce the accused
at the next hearing which will take place at 2 p.m.
November 25. The representatives of the Bureau of Public
Safety requested the extradition of the accused.
At the request of the Bureau of Public Safety,
the French Municipal Police have arrested Miss Sze Liang
(史良), a lawyer, Mr. Chow Tao Feng (鄒奮), Editor-
in-Chief of the "Livelihood Sunday Weekly", and Mr. Chang
Nan Chi (章乃器), an economist, on a similar charge.
The arrested persons were arraigned before
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court at 3 p.m.
November 23. Messrs. Chang Tse Niang (張志讓) and Tong Hwa
(唐豪) are appearing for Mr. Chang Nan Chi and Miss Sze
Liang; Mr. Sung Tso Chi (孫祖基) for Mr. Chow Tao Feng.
It is learned that they will likewise be released on bail.
The following information was secured from the
families of the various accused by a reporter of this paper:-

November 24, 1936. Morning Translation.

Mr. Wang Chao Shih resides at No. 7
Tifeng Road. When our reporter called, only Mr. Wang's
mother and his six-year old son were at home. Mr. Wang
was arrested at 3 a.m. November 23. He offered no
objection to his arrest after he was shown an official
document by the three police officers who had come to
arrest him.

The home of Mr. Sung Chung Shih is
located at No. 51, Tao Yuen Villa (桃源村), Yuyuen Road.
When the five police officers called on the morning of
November 23, he was fast asleep. The officers were
admitted into the house by a servant. One of the officers
remained on guard outside the house, one in the hall, while
the other three followed the servant upstairs. Upon
learning of the arrest, the elder son of Mr. Sung Chung
Shih, who lives at house No. 53 in the same alleyway,
immediately called at his father's home. Both the father
and the son were shown the official despatch from the
Bureau of Public Safety. After a brief consultation with
his son, Mr. Sung Chung Shih left with the officers.

Mr. Li Kung Pu resides at No. 24 Han
Chong Li (亨昌里) off Yuyuen Road. When the police
officers arrived at 2 a.m. November 23, Mr. Li happened
to be out with friends. The officers remained in the
house until about 2.30 a.m. when Mr. Li returned and was
placed under arrest.

The residence of lawyer Soo Chi Lien is
situate at No. 14, Lane No. 524, Avenue Road. When the
police officers arrived, he was in bed.

Mr. Chang Nan Chi resides at No. 24
Shih Wei Li (施卫里) off Route Delastre, French Concession.
Officers of the French Police, accompanied by members of
the Bureau of Public Safety, arrived at the place at 2 a.m.
November 23. They climbed over a short bamboo fence
outside the front gate and were admitted into the house
by the inmates. They immediately proceeded upstairs and
showing Mr. Chang the official document, they placed him
under arrest.

Lawyer Sze Liang lives at No. 1 Lafayette
Villa, Rue Lafayette. At first the foreign and Chinese
detectives could not effect an entrance either from the
front or the back gate, because the inmates refused to
open the door for fear of robbers. The officers then
climbed over the short wall in front of the main gate and
effected an entry into the main hall from where they
immediately proceeded upstairs. Upon being shown
the official document, lawyer Sze Liang at once dressed
herself and left with the officers.

Mr. Chow Tao Feng lives at No. 1, Lane
No. 601, Rue Lafayette. The police officers were admitted
by himself. One of the members of the Bureau of Public
Safety then said to him: "I have been shadowing you for
three days and saw you returning home in a ricksha at about
11 p.m. November 22. I immediately notified the French
Police and we have now come to arrest you." The police
officers then seized several English books which they took
to the Station for examination.

November 13, 1936.

Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation Federation
- convenes meetings in celebration of the birthday of
the late Kuomintang Leader.

The Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Federation convened a meeting of members of local national
salvation associations in the Chinese Y.W.C.A., 999 Bubbling
Well Road, at 1 p.m. November 12, ostensibly to celebrate the
birthday of the late Kuomintang leader Dr. Sun Yat-sen.

A large number of Chinese consisting of students,
labourers and shop assistants proceeded to the Ningpo Fellow
Countrymen's Association, 480 Yu Ya Ching Road, between 12
noon and 1 p.m. November 12, but upon arrival there were
informed by pickets that the Police and officials of the
Association had forbidden the meeting there, and were instructed
to proceed to the Chinese Y.W.C.A., the second meeting place.
By 2 p.m. about 800 persons had entered the compound of the
Y.W.C.A. and at that time the meeting was formally opened.
A presidium consisting of the following persons was formed :-

Li Kung-poh (李公樸), Principal of the Liang Zai
Supplementary School, Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road, and one of the leading
members of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association.

Tsang Mai-chi (章乃器), ex-Sub-Manager of the Chekiang
Industrial Bank, and a leading member of the
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.

Wong Chao-dzu (王造時), a lawyer by profession,
living at 7B Tifeng Road, a leading member of the
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.

Sung Chun-dzu (沈鈞儒), a lawyer by profession, living
at 5 Tao Yuan Fang, Yu Yuen Road, and concurrently
Dean of the Shanghai Law College, Kiangwan Road. He
is a leading member of the Cultural Circles National
Salvation Association.

Sz Liang (史良), a female lawyer, living at 1
Lafayette Terrace, Rue Lafayette. A leading member
of the Women's Circles National Salvation Association.

Soo Chien-li (沙千里), a lawyer by profession with
an office at the Tsung Chen (宗誠) Building,
Kiukiang Road. A committee member of the Ants' Club
(Ants' Club), Room 420 Continental Emporium Building,
Nanking Road, and concurrently a leading member of
the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association.

- 2 -

Yang Ching-sai (楊經才), a supervisor in the Tien Yih
(天一) Insurance Company, 255 Peking Road. A
leading member of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association.

After the formal opening of the meeting, those
present sang two songs entitled "March of Volunteer Armies
(義勇軍進行曲) and "Beat them back home" (打回老家去)
(the latter song is anti-Japanese in nature). Li Kung-poh
then made a speech eulogizing the deeds and spirit of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen. He stated that the object of the meeting
apart from celebrating the anniversary was to induce the
authorities to cease concluding secret agreements with Japan
and advocated that the nation should be saved in accordance
with the instructions of the late leader.

The second speaker was Tsang Hai-chi, who stated
that China should unite with Great Britain, the United States,
France and Soviet Russia and form a group to ensure the safety
of China against Japan.

Wong Chao-dzu followed, and made a speech stating
that the late Kuomintang leader advocated that a treaty should
be concluded with Soviet Russia, that the Communist Party
should be allowed in China, and agriculture and industry should
be developed. He continued to say that the present Chinese
Government had ignored these instructions and therefore China
suffered from foreign aggression.

Sung Chun-dzu (沈鈞儒) was the next speaker. He
also advocated the policies mentioned above as the means to
save China from ruin. He also remarked that Dr. Sun Yat-sen
had praised Lenin and as conditions in Soviet Russia were
had
excellent, Dr. Sun Yat-sen/been right. He said that no power
in the world could break Soviet Russia. He concluded that
China should unite with the Communist Party in compliance
with the instructions of Dr. Sun. He was of the opinion that
the Government should forthwith suspend the anti-Communist
campaign.

- 3 -

Sz Liang was the fifth speaker. She stated that the
Chinese Government should not prohibit the people from taking
part in the national salvation movement at the present
critical time and that all the Chinese irrespective of parties
should unanimously resist Japan. She remarked that according
to the instructions of Dr. Sun, the Government should protect
the people in the national salvation movement but the present
government, she continued, not only refrained from protecting
the people, but oppressed them.

At this point, an invitation was issued to those
present to deliver speeches. Two female workers named Fang
Dzu (方 氏) and Liu Tsao-dee (劉招弟), claiming to be in the
employ of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, accepted the invitation.
Fang Dzu reported that the workers of Japanese cotton mills
had gone on strike to demand an increase in wages and that some
workers had been taken to a small room by the Japanese
management. She described that one of these workers had been
killed by the Japanese and her body put in a sack and thrown
into the Wangpoo. At this juncture, the audience commenced
to shout slogans including "Overthrow the Japanese Imperialists"
and "Assist the Strikers." Liu Tsao-dee, the next speaker,
made another speech depicting how the workers were cruelly
exploited by the capitalists and requested the attendance to
render assistance to the workers.

Tsang Kai-chi again took the platform and informed
the crowd that Madame Sun Yat-sen had intended to be present
to deliver a speech, but was prevented by illness. He read
the following speech written by her.

"In commemoration of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, brethren
throughout the nation should continue to struggle for the
emancipation of the Chinese race. At present, we should
realize that our greatest enemies are the Japanese
Imperialists and Chinese traitors."

- 4 -

"We should unite with all nations who are lovers of
peace and form an international league against invasion,
especially by allying with Great Britain, U.S.A., France,
and Soviet Russia to ensure collective safety on the Pacific
and to oppose the Japanese imperialists. We should ally
with the peace-loving masses of Japan, Korea and Formosa
and form a united international battle line to overthrow the
Fascist militarists of Japan. We should unite all parties
and classes to form a united battle line for the purpose of
overthrowing the Japanese imperialists.

"The three policies of Dr. Sun indicate the above
plans. We should go forward bravely. Steel and blood
will certainly accomplish the glorious enterprise for the
emancipation of the race."

Tsang Nai-chi concluded by saying that the people
should of their own accord rise and save their nation despite
obstruction from the Government.

Wong Chao-dz then took the platform and read the
following proposals to the crowd, which were duly passed :
1) That the attendance should contribute money to support
the strikers of Japanese cotton mills.
2) That the Government be requested to cease concluding secret
agreements with Japan, but to send troops to the North
to assist the anti-Japanese troops at Suiyuan.
3) That a delegation be appointed to proceed to the North
and to convey good wishes to the anti-Japanese armies at
Suiyuan.
4) That the Government be requested to unite with Great
Britain, United States of America, France and Soviet Russia
and form an international league against Japan.

- 5 -

5) That a circular telegram be despatched informing
the people throughout China of the minutes of this
meeting.
Wong Chao-dzu then submitted to the meeting the
following proposals made by the Shanghai Municipality
Students Circles National Salvation Association :-
1) That the Government release all students arrested
in connection with the national salvation Movement.
2) That the authorities of various universities be
induced to take back those students dismissed in
connection with the national salvation movement.
3) That the Government be urged to enforce special
education during times of national crisis.
The following resolutions proposed by members
of the audience were then discussed and passed :-
1) That funds be raised by public subscription on behalf
of the strikers in a three days' campaign commencing
on November 13.
2) That Groups be formed to sympathize with the strikers
in Japanese cotton mills.
3) That a demand be submitted for the release of workers
arrested in connection with the strike in Japanese
cotton mills, failing which a general strike be
declared.
4) That the General Labour Union be requested to call
for a strike of all labourers in Shanghai, in sympathy
with the Japanese cotton mill strikers.
5) That a "Japanese Mill Strikers' Support Committee" be
formed consisting of two representatives from each local
public body.

- 6 -
6. That a circular telegram be despatched asking Chinese
at home and abroad to render assistance to the strikers
in Japanese cotton mills.
7. That anti-Japanese propaganda groups be formed in
connection with the strike of the Japanese cotton mills.
8. That the anti-Communist campaign undertaken by the
National Government be opposed.
Finally it was decided to refer all these regulations
to the members of the presidium for execution. The meeting
was concluded at 4 p.m. when the following slogans were shouted:-
1. Support the anti-Japanese troops in Suiyuan.
2. Urge the government to issue a general mobilization
order at once in order to resist Japan.
3. Oppose the co-operation of China and Japan in the anti-
communist campaign, and demand the immediate suspension
of the communist suppression campaign.
4. Ally with Great Britain, U.S.A., France and Soviet Russia
to ensure collective safety on the Pacific.
5. Unite various parties in the country to resist foreign
aggression.
6. Let Chinese and Japanese masses unite and overthrow the
Japanese Imperialists.
7. Urge the Kuomintang to restore the National revolutionary
spirit of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
8. Oppose the Government's connivance at the Japanese
invasion into North China.
9. The revolutionary spirit of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen
is immortal !
10. Long live the emancipation of the Republic of China.

- 7 -

While the crowd which towards the close of the
meeting numbered approximately 1,000 persons was dispersing,
persons were posted at an inner gate of the Y.M.C.A. premises
and collected subscriptions in support of the strikers of
Japanese cotton mills. A total sum of $200 was raised.

During the proceedings, copies of two kinds of
literature were distributed among the attendance. One is
entitled "Special Issue of the National Salvation Intelligence
in commemoration of the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen."
It contains the speech of Madame Sun Yat-sen and the ten slogans
referred to above. The other, a handbill, contains a
manifesto purporting to emanate from the Shanghai Municipality
Students Circles National Salvation Association bearing on the
commemoration of the birthday of the late Kuomintang leader.
This handbill advocates that the Government should

1. Carry out Dr. Sun's revolutionary policies.
2. Assist the anti-Japanese troops at Suiyuan.
3. Enforce "Too Yuan" (?) diplomacy.
4. Protect the freedom of patriotic movements.

Also present at the meeting were ten plain-clothes
members of the Bureau of Public Safety and Mr. and Mrs. Max
Granich. Max Granich is the editor of the reactionary
publication entitled "Voice of China."

A. On the afternoon on or about 12-11-36, several police officers came to our Guild and asked us if we had granted anyone to use our hall to hold a meeting, and I answered in the negative. This Court has been requested by the Kiangsu High Court to ask

Sung Chung Lu stated that on the 31-5-36, a meeting was held at

Q. Is your association situated on Yuen Ming Yuen Rd?

knowledge. If there was a large number of people attending to the
meeting, we must know it. We have questioned our watchman and
several coolies, and they said that no meeting was held on that
day, which was a holiday.
